title: Business Process Reengineering: A Bibliometric Study
summary: Business Process Reengineering (BPR) has become an important research domain for understanding organizational transformation, process improvement, and technology-driven change. This study aims to examine the intellectual structure, research development, influential contributions, and emerging themes in BPR literature through a bibliometric analysis approach. Data were collected from the Scopus database using relevant keywords related to Business Process Reengineering, and the retrieved publications were analyzed using VOSviewer to identify citation patterns, collaboration networks, keyword co-occurrence, thematic evolution, and research density. The findings indicate that BPR research has developed through several major knowledge streams, including process optimization, information systems integration, organizational change, enterprise resource planning, and supply chain management. Citation analysis reveals that influential studies have primarily focused on the relationship between information technology, process redesign, and successful implementation strategies. The keyword analysis demonstrates that BPR has evolved from a traditional efficiency-oriented approach toward a broader transformation framework involving digital technologies, organizational capabilities, and strategic adaptation. Furthermore, collaboration analysis highlights the contribution of leading researchers, institutions, and countries in shaping the development of BPR knowledge. This study contributes by providing a comprehensive overview of BPR research evolution and identifying future research opportunities related to artificial intelligence, automation, Industry 4.0, and digital transformation.

title: A qualitative study of sustainability oriented financial decision making and gender equity among working-age women in Thailand
summary: Thai working-age women possess deep, culturally embedded sustainability values derived from Buddhist philosophical traditions and the Sufficiency Economy Philosophy, yet face systematic structural exclusion from sustainable investment markets. This qualitative study recruited 35 working-age women (25–55 years) from Bangkok’s diverse employment sectors and conducted in-depth, semi-structured interviews in 2024, which were transcribed verbatim, professionally translated, and analyzed using Braun and Clarke’s reflexive thematic analysis framework. The study identified a profound values-behavior gap: 91% of participants articulated strong environmental sustainability values, 94% expressed clear interest in sustainable finance when concepts were explained, yet 0% currently engaged with any sustainable investment instrument. Analysis reveals this exclusion is structural rather than preference-based, with synergistic barriers including capital constraints (83%), knowledge deficits (86%), limited mainstream product availability (89%), and gender-specific household decision-making restrictions (69%). The research demonstrates that sustainable finance accessibility in Thailand requires fractional micro-investing mechanisms, mandatory mainstream bank distribution requirements, Thai-language financial education, and integrated household financial empowerment programs. The study advances sustainable finance theory by establishing gender equity and environmental sustainability as structurally inseparable and simultaneously addressable policy imperatives. Future research should examine policy implementation outcomes and regional applicability across Southeast Asian economies facing comparable gender-sustainability finance dynamics.

title: The Forced Interior Black Hole Radiation from Ledger Accounting
summary: Double-entry bookkeeping, taken as a finite substrate for physics, gives an exact account of black hole evaporation. A ledger of d accounts posts one unit per tick; the record of postings is the radiation. The ledger's arrow of time selects black holes over their reverses. The visible record's capacity to name what is still hidden overtakes the interior's capacity to hide it exactly at the midpoint of the evaporation, by pure counting, and the entropy of the visible record rises to its peak there and returns to zero: the Page curve, with no ensemble and no averaging. The main theorem is about information return: any exterior readout from which the infalling history can be recovered resolves the interior completely, so an evaporation that gives the record back cannot also keep an unresolved inside. Every step is machine-checked in Lean 4. The account consumes one physical law (a one-sided record-area law, which fixes the Bekenstein quarter), a six-line dictionary, and two units constants, an entropy scale c and a per-tick energy quantum E_0, which the ledger provably cannot select. It predicts no dimensionful number.

title: Auditing Symbolic-Law Sharing: A Failure-Aware Benchmark for Multi-Environment Scientific Regression
summary: Preprint (v0.6). Not peer-reviewed.Scientific law discovery often pools related experiments to identify shared symbolic structure and then adapts a few environment-specific parameters. Pooling can compensate for limited observations, but a poor sharing decision may fit low-range support and still fail in an unseen environment’s tail. We introduce a failure-aware, target-access-controlled benchmark for auditing symbolic transfer across held-out scientific environments. Its inventory covers five real scientific assets; a retrospective global-versus-restricted ledger covers four through 18 dependent contrasts while retaining invalid-domain predictions, failed repetitions, finite catastrophes, protocol timing, and redistribution boundaries. The evidence is deliberately mixed: global sharing and restrictions based on archives, cohorts, geometry, or machining conditions each help in some settings and harm in others. We also audit one frozen source only validation policy over 196 dependent environment-family units from the same four ledger assets. It improves equal-dataset cap-2 mean action regret relative to always-global, but selects seven failed arms versus three, and only 6 of 14 dataset-family cells have a positive score-benefit rank direction. These results expose a conflict between average transfer utility and failure safety. They motivate a minimum reporting contract that separates source-side arm selection, held-out support fitting, and tail evaluation, and reports utility, failures, coverage, and protocol validity separately. The contribution is an evaluation and audit framework, not calibrated abstention or a universally superior symbolic-regression family.

title: Shareholder activism and securities regulation in India: A comparative study of SEBI, the SEC, and the FCA
summary: Shareholder activism has become a central mechanism of corporate governance, yet the regulatory frameworks that enable it vary sharply across jurisdictions. This article examines the regulatory architecture governing shareholder activism in India and evaluates it against two mature securities market regulators, the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the United Kingdom Financial Conduct Authority (FCA). Using a doctrinal, black letter method grounded in legislation, regulatory guidelines, case law, and peer reviewed literature, the study compares regulatory design, enforcement culture, and institutional engagement across the three jurisdictions. It finds that shareholder activism in India remains at an early, largely reactive stage of development, constrained by concentrated promoter ownership, limited retail investor awareness, procedural delay, and comparatively weak enforcement relative to the SEC's enforcement driven model and the FCA's stewardship based model. Reforms under the Companies Act, 2013 and successive regulations of the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) have nonetheless measurably improved disclosure, e voting, minority protection, and institutional engagement. Because existing scholarship on shareholder activism concentrates heavily on advanced markets, this article contributes a structured three way comparison of SEBI, the SEC, and the FCA specifically oriented toward activism, and proposes India specific reforms that selectively draw on both enforcement based and stewardship based regulatory traditions.

title: Information and Communication Technology (ICT) as a determinant of accounting processes in telecommunication firms (A study of Globacom)
summary: This study investigates the role of information and communication technology (ICT) as a determinant of accounting processes in telecommunications firms, with focus on GLOBACOM Nigeria. The research aims to explore how ICT adoption influences accounting efficiency, accuracy and reliability, while also identifying the tools used, challenges encountered and opportunities created. The study employed a quantitative research approach using structured questionnaires administered to accounting professionals within GLOBACOM. Data were analysed using the chi-square statistical method to test three of four hypotheses and a descriptive classification was used under hypothesis two. The results revealed a significant relationship between ICT adoption and improved accounting performance. Findings showed that GLOBACOM makes use of various ICT tools such as ERP systems, accounting software, spreadsheets, and communication platforms. However, financial hurdles and staff resistance were noted as challenges. On the other hand, ICT adoption facilitated better reporting, enhanced decision making, and improved productivity. The study concludes that ICT is a powerful enabler of accounting transformation in telecommunications sector. It recommends investing in staff training, strategic budgeting, infrastructure upgrades, and effective change management to, maximize the benefit of ICT. This research contributes valuable insights into the growing intersection between technology and financial management. Keywords: Information, Technology, Globacom, Accounting, Processess.

title: THE EFFECT OF GREEN ACCOUNTING, LEVERAGE, AND FIRM SIZE ON SUSTAINABILITY REPORT DISCLOSURE
summary: Purpose: This study examines the effect of green accounting, leverage, and firm size on sustainability report (SR) disclosure among agribusiness companies in the Consumer Non-Cyclicals sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2021–2025. The study is grounded in legitimacy theory and agency theory. Research Methodology: This quantitative explanatory study uses secondary data from annual reports and sustainability reports. Purposive sampling selected 10 companies and generated 50 initial firm-year observations. Green accounting is measured by the ratio of environmental cost to net profit, leverage by the Debt to Asset Ratio (DAR), firm size by the natural logarithm of total assets, and SR disclosure by the Sustainability Report Disclosure Index (SRDI) based on the applicable GRI Standards. The data were analyzed using pooled multiple linear regression with IBM SPSS Statistics 26. A Cochrane–Orcutt transformation was applied after the initial model indicated autocorrelation. Results: Green accounting has a positive and significant association with SR disclosure (t = 2.594; Sig. = 0.013). Leverage is not statistically significant (t = −0.439; Sig. = 0.663). Firm size has a positive and significant association with SR disclosure (t ≈ 3.87; Sig. < 0.001) and the largest standardized coefficient. The overall model is significant (F = 7.667; Sig. < 0.001), while its explanatory power is moderate, with an Adjusted R² of 0.294. Conclusions: SR disclosure in the sampled companies is more closely associated with environmental-cost intensity and organizational capacity than with debt structure. Limitations: The findings are limited by the small purposive sample, the use of pooled regression for firm-year data, the non-identical coverage of GRI 2016 and GRI 2021 indicators, the positive-net-profit selection criterion, and the absence of an independent coding-reliability test. Contributions: The study contributes sector-specific evidence by operationalizing green accounting through an environmental-cost ratio rather than a disclosure dummy and by identifying implications for managers, investors, and regulators

title: The impact of digital communication strategies on the effectiveness of strategic planning in financial auditing firms in the Kingdom of Bahrain
summary: This study aims to examine the extent of adopting digital communication strategies (information, persuasion, dialogue, and consensus-building strategies), evaluate the level of strategic planning effectiveness, and assess the overall impact of digital communication strategies on strategic planning effectiveness within financial audit firms in the Kingdom of Bahrain. To achieve these objectives, the study employed a descriptive -analytical methodology. Primary data were collected using a structured questionnaire administered to a survey sample of (50) professionals in Bahraini audit firms (66% male, 34% female; 70% holding a Bachelor's degree). The statistical analysis revealed that financial audit firms utilize digital communication strategies at a high level of effectiveness, with an overall relative importance of (78%). The "dialogue strategy" ranked first (78.8%), followed by the "information strategy" (78%), "consensus-building strategy" (77.4%), and "persuasion strategy" (75.8%). Furthermore, strategic planning effectiveness scored high, with a relative importance of (75.6%). Multiple regression analysis confirmed a statistically significant impact of digital communication strategies combined on strategic planning effectiveness (R = 0.556, F = 77.974, p < 0.01). Specifically, consensus -building, information, and persuasion strategies showed statistically significant individual impacts, whereas the dialogue strategy did not show a direct significant impact in the regression model. Based on these findings, the study recommends enhancing the quality of digital data provided to stakeholders, refining media messaging clarity, and aligning digital communication processes to foster institutional synergy and audience trust.

summary: Accounting is a fundamental subject in commerce education, but many students admitted to the traditional B.Com. programme have a weak understanding of basic accounting concepts. This creates difficulty in learning Financial Accounting and affects their academic performance. The present study aims to examine the level of foundational accounting knowledge among B. Com students and to identify the need for remedial measures to improve their conceptual clarity. The study is empirical in nature and is based on primary data collected from 100 B. Com students from selected colleges in Navi Mumbai. A structured questionnaire and a basic diagnostic test were used for data collection. The study focuses on core topics such as journal, ledger, trial balance and final accounts. The collected data is analysed using percentage and tabular methods. The study is expected to show that many students lack basic accounting knowledge and require bridge courses and remedial teaching. The findings will help teachers and institutions to develop strategies to strengthen the foundation of accounting education.

title: Bridging the Foundational Gap in Accounting Education: An Empirical Study of B. Com Students
summary: Abstract Accounting is a fundamental subject in commerce education, but many students admitted to the traditional B.Com. programme have a weak understanding of basic accounting concepts. This creates difficulty in learning Financial Accounting and affects their academic performance. The present study aims to examine the level of foundational accounting knowledge among B. Com students and to identify the need for remedial measures to improve their conceptual clarity. The study is empirical in nature and is based on primary data collected from 100 B. Com students from selected colleges in Navi Mumbai. A structured questionnaire and a basic diagnostic test were used for data collection. The study focuses on core topics such as journal, ledger, trial balance and final accounts. The collected data is analysed using percentage and tabular methods. The study is expected to show that many students lack basic accounting knowledge and require bridge courses and remedial teaching. The findings will help teachers and institutions to develop strategies to strengthen the foundation of accounting education.

title: A Course-Anchored Capability Audit of GitHub Copilot for Introductory Programming: Specification and Code Generation - Companion Material
summary: Companion material associated with the work "A Course-Anchored Capability Audit of GitHub Copilot for Introductory Programming: Specification and Code Generation". This deposit provides the artifacts required to inspect and reproduce the reported course-anchored capability audit of GitHub Copilot. It includes the 14 introductory C++ programming tasks used in the study, instructor-authored reference implementations and specifications, the original Spanish code-generation prompts together with English translations, the operational scoring rubrics, adjudicated slot-level scoring records for specification and code generation, and supplementary figures and numerical summaries. The study evaluates generated artifacts rather than student learning outcomes. The materials therefore support auditing of GitHub Copilot's availability, non-repetition, specification accuracy, functional correctness, curricular-boundary compliance, redundancy, correction effort, and variability across repeated runs. One run corresponds to one complete execution of a fixed prompt requesting up to ten candidate alternatives. The numerical entries in the preserved scoring records are unchanged from the original study records.

title: Digital Public Infrastructure, Instant Payments and Financial Inclusion: Comparing Nigeria and Kenya with India and Brazil
summary: This article compares digital public infrastructure (DPI), instant payment systems and financial inclusion outcomes in Nigeria and Kenya with those of India and Brazil. Using secondary data from the World Bank Global Findex 2025, Remittance Prices Worldwide, IMF assessments, NPCI, Banco Central do Brasil and peer-reviewed sources, it examines why Nigeria’s eNaira and expanding national identity system have not produced usage levels comparable to India’s Unified Payments Interface (UPI) or Brazil’s Pix, while Kenya achieved high account ownership through mobile money without a retail CBDC. Key findings show large gaps in adult account ownership (Kenya 90.1%, India 89.0%, Brazil 86.4%, Nigeria 63.3%), transaction scale, and remittance costs. The analysis concludes that interoperability, merchant incentives and government-to-person payment routing, rather than the mere launch of a central bank digital currency, drive inclusion at scale. Policy recommendations focus on bank–fintech–mobile-money interoperability, G2P routing, and cheaper formal remittance corridors for Nigeria and other African economies.

title: Plan for Every Part (PFEP): A Strategic Blueprint for Advanced Part Planning and Precision Safety Stock Optimization
summary: Global supply chain volatility and fragmented master data frequently force manufacturing organizations to rely on static, blanket inventory heuristics. These legacy approaches result in systemic operational inefficiencies, characterized by high working capital carrying costs on one end and assembly line-side stockouts on the other. This white paper presents a comprehensive operational architecture combining the Plan for Every Part (PFEP) methodology with advanced, variable-driven safety stock sizing models. By unifying static material attributes, dynamic lead time variances, and line-side delivery parameters into a centralized repository, PFEP establishes a single source of truth for component management. The paper details the application of dual-variable ABC-XYZ inventory segmentation to tailor replenishment strategies based on part valuation and demand predictability. Furthermore, it outlines a rigorous mathematical safety stock model that accounts for simultaneous variability in both daily demand consumption (σD) and supplier lead times (σL), proving that traditional rule-of-thumb buffers under-protect volatile components while over-capitalizing stable ones. Finally, a three-phase execution roadmap- covering data standardization, automated platform recalculation, and closed-loop governance- is presented to guide operations leaders in significant inventory cost reductions in inventory carrying costs while maintaining superior line-side availability.

title: INFLATION-ADJUSTED SUSTAINABILITY IN BANKING: ANALYSIS OF WATER CONSUMPTION, CARBON EMISSIONS, AND FINANCIAL INDICATORS IN TURKISH BANKS
summary: This study evaluates the sustainability performance of Turkish banks by analyzing water consumption, carbon emissions, and financial indicators from 2019 to 2024. Using publicly available sustainability reports, the research examines key environmental and financial metrics, including CDP scores, Scope 1-3 emissions, and inflation-adjusted financial ratios. A Cumulative Inflation Adjustment method is applied to financial data to ensure comparability across years. The findings indicate that Turkish banks have improved sustainability disclosures and increased efficiency in financial operations relative to emissions and water consumption. However, data adjusted for cumulative inflation reveal that there has not been a significant improvement in banks' sustainability policies, and in some cases, even a decline has been observed. Notably, banks that have adopted renewable energy sources have achieved substantial reductions in Scope 2 emissions, whereas financed emissions (Scope 3) remain a critical challenge. The results highlight the need for stronger ESG integration, standardized sustainability reporting, and long-term environmental risk mitigation strategies to enhance the resilience of the Turkish banking sector in a high-inflation.
